messages:
Maria: Quick perf dump from the continuous-batching kernel sweep across regions :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Maria: Ran the same Llama-variant (7B) with three kernel stacks: auto, prefer_fp16, int8-quant. Tests across us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast. 90th/99th and throughput numbers attached (see dashboard link).
Maria: Short summary: int8 on H100 gives best cost/throughput in us-west (median 16ms, 99p 42ms, sustained 1.9k tokens/s per GPU). A100 fp16 is ~28ms median, 99p 75ms. ap-southeast showed 2–3x tail spikes depending on kernel.
Maria: Biggest surprise: kernel auto-selection sometimes picks fp16 kernels on H100 for long sequences which increases 99p latency vs forcing int8. Seems tied to sequence length threshold in kernel selector.
Maria: Config used for the sweep:```
server.scheduler: continuous
server.batch_window_ms: 12
server.max_batch_tokens: 8192
server.fairness_weight: 0.5
model.kernel_policy: auto
model.kernel_overrides: {"prefer_fp16_threshold": 1024}
```
Alex: Nice writeup. Do you have the per-client fairness metric? wondering if fairness_weight 0.5 starves low-qps clients. :eyes:
Maria: Yes — we logged per_client_wait_ms and per_client_batch_share. In us-west fairness 0.5 kept tail latency okay while preserving throughput. In ap-southeast increasing fairness to 0.8 cut 99p per-client wait by ~45ms but reduced overall throughput ~6%.
Jordan: Quick micro-experiment: bumped batch_window_ms from 12 -> 20 and dropped max_batch_tokens to 4096. Result: smoother latency (lower 99p jitter) but throughput dropped 8% on A100. So there's a tradeoff.
Sam: Did you test window smoothing or exponential decay for the scheduler? iirc continuous batcher has a smoothing factor that affects how it aggregates small clients.
Maria: Yes — we tried smoothing_alpha 0.6 vs 0.9. alpha=0.9 reacts faster to bursts (lower median), alpha=0.6 reduces spikes for small clients. Our recommendation: alpha=0.75 as a compromise for global defaults.
Sam: For kernels, can we change kernel_policy to `prefer_int8_on_h100` for rollout? Might avoid auto doing fp16 on long seqs.
Maria: That's the plan. For Dedicated we can set model.kernel_overrides per-host-type. For hosted API we want a safe default flag: `kernel_heuristic: region-aware` which prefers int8 on H100 in us-west/eu-west and falls back to fp16 in ap-southeast to avoid device-specific slow paths.
perf-bot: perf-bot: scheduled cylinder job: kernel-sweep-1767403200 finished. Artifacts: s3://redwood-perf/kernel-sweep/1767403200/*.png and csv.
ci-bot: ci-bot: nightly-bench->compare:H100-int8 vs A100-fp16 -> diff report at https://dash.internal/redwood/bench/1767403200 (password-protected).
Alex: Two follow ups: (1) add a rollout canary with region=ap-southeast only, (2) add an alert when kernel auto-selection changes for a model (so we can triage regressions quickly).
Maria: Adding both to the plan. Also going to add a Console metric: `model.kernel_choice_change_count` and expose it per-route.
Jordan: One more note: KV-cache warmup in ap-southeast is exposing an implementation detail — the cache miss cost is amplified when kernel switch causes additional memory churn. We'll instrument memory allocs during kernel-switch.
Maria: Agreed. Action items:
- Maria: push kernel_heuristic prototype to staging by EOD Tue
- Alex: setup canary rollout (ap-southeast) and alert rule by Wed
- Jordan: add memory alloc traces + attach to perf artifacts
- Sam: update default scheduler config to batch_window_ms=15, smoothing_alpha=0.75, max_batch_tokens=6144
Maria: Thanks all — attaching short screenshot + CSV in perf-bot artifacts. If no objections we'll flip kernel_heuristic to prefer_int8_on_h100 for the staged rollout. :thumbsup:
